Replay \'D\' → decode → [\'D\'].\n\nOK, root cause confirmed: after the last step of an incomplete replay, mode remains \'REPLAYING\' forever. In `handleReplayTimeout`, when `wellStateId + 1` is not in the replay, there\'s no transition to PLAYING.\n\nNote: the existing test "lets you undo and stops replaying when a replay is in progress" (lines 378–396) replays \'AAAA AAAA AAAA\' (12 moves) and advances 60 steps. After the fix, mode will become PLAYING after 12 steps; undo works in PLAYING. This test currently passes, and will still pass after the fix.\n\nBut note: after the fix, once mode becomes PLAYING, further advanceReplaySteps timeouts are… since the last step set `nextReplayTimeoutId` to undefined, no more timeouts are scheduled. Good.\n\nAlso note: if a replay ends with the game ending (GAME_OVER), mode must remain GAME_OVER. handleMove sets the mode to GAME_OVER. So in handleReplayTimeout, after the redo, check `this.state.mode`:\n\n```ts\nlet nextMode = mode\n\nif (mode === \'REPLAYING\') {\n  await this.handleRedo()\n\n  if (wellStateId + 1 in replay) {\n    nextReplayTimeoutId = setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)\n  } else if (this.state.mode !== \'GAME_OVER\') {\n    // Replay is over: hand control back to the player\n    nextMode = \'PLAYING\'\n  }\n} else {\n  console.warn(...)\n}\n\nthis.setState({\n  mode: nextMode,\n  replayTimeoutId: nextReplayTimeoutId\n})\n```\n\nHmm — setState always sets mode: nextMode, and if it\'s not the last step, nextMode = mode (unchanged). Fine.\n\nWait: another subtle issue — the `console.warn(\'Ignoring redo event because end of history has been reached\')` inside handleRedo. When does handleRedo get called when wellStateId is not in the replay? Only in the last step case… no wait: handleReplayTimeout only schedules a timeout when `wellStateId+1 in replay`, so at the time of the call wellStateId is always in the replay. The "end of history" warning inside handleRedo fires via Ctrl+Y. OK.\n\nNext, coverage: 100% branch coverage is required. New branch: `else if (this.state.mode !== \'GAME_OVER\')` — both sides need to be covered:\n1. {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'A very interesting failure:\n\n1. `\'lets you replay a too-long replay\'` (an existing test!) failed with the following error:\n```\nError: Can\'t get next well state if there is no piece in the well\n  at getNextState (logic.ts:108)\n  at Object.handleMove (logic.ts:327)\n  at Game.handleMove (Game.tsx:132)\n  at Game.handleRedo (Game.tsx:339)\n  at Timeout.handleReplayTimeout (Game.tsx:249)\n```\n\nSo, during replay of 48 L moves, at the point when the well no longer has a live piece, handleRedo was called — i.e., after game over… no wait. "no piece in the well" — when a piece is locked, handleMove replaces it with a new piece unless GAME_OVER. So piece === null only when… after the piece is locked on the final move? Let me think.\n\nHmm, wait — in the game-over case, after the game-over move, the piece should be non-null (the piece that overflowed)? Actually, game over is detected when the locked piece reached row bar-1. The piece that caused game over: in getNextState, when \'D\' moves into a blocked state, nextPiece = null, well is updated. Then handleMove: nextWellState.piece === null && nextMode === \'GAME_OVER\' → no new piece → piece stays null.\n\nSo after the game-over move, wellStates[last].piece === null.\n\nThen, why did the too-long replay test reach handleRedo in a state with no piece? Sequence: the game ends on move 47 (index 46, per my earlier analysis). After that, the timeout at step 47: mode should be GAME_OVER → warn. But the error indicates that handleRedo was called at Game.tsx:249 — `await this.handleRedo()` — i.e., mode was REPLAYING at step 47, and replay[47] = \'L\' was applied → handleMove → getNextState(wellStates[47]?)…\n\nWait a sec. Why is the mode still REPLAYING at that point? With my fix… no wait, my fix doesn\'t change the mode in non-exhausted steps. Hmm, but wait — did this test fail before my fix too?? No — in the pre-fix full-file run, this test passed (✔ too-long 3734ms). Now it fails. What in my fix could affect this?\n\nMy change: setState now also includes `mode: nextMode`. On non-exhausted steps, nextMode = mode (stale \'REPLAYING\'). Same as before (before, setState didn\'t touch mode). No behavior change…\n\nWait, actually — the issue might be timing/ordering of state updates. Before the fix: handleReplayTimeout did setState({replayTimeoutId}) after the redo. The redo\'s setState (from handleMove) set mode GAME_OVER. Then handleReplayTimeout\'s setState({replayTimeoutId: undefined}) — no mode → mode stays GAME_OVER.\n\nAfter my fix: handleReplayTimeout does setState({mode: nextMode, replayTimeoutId}). In the exhausted case, nextMode = \'GAME_OVER\' (via the ternary, this.state.mode). Same.\n\nIn the non-exhausted case, nextMode = stale \'REPLAYING\'. If the redo\'s move ended the game, mode should become GAME_OVER — but my setState overwrites it with \'REPLAYING\'!!!\n\nThat\'s the bug in my fix! On the step where the game ends but the replay still has moves left (the too-long case), nextMode = stale \'REPLAYING\' → overwrites GAME_OVER → replay continues → handleRedo on the next step with mode REPLAYING → handleMove with piece null → throws!\n\nSo the ternary is only in the exhausted branch. In the non-exhausted branch, I also have to use the new mode. Fix: use `this.state.mode` in all places:\n\n```ts\nif (wellStateId + 1 in replay) {\n  nextReplayTimeoutId = setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)\n} \nnextMode = this.state.mode === \'REPLAYING\' ? \'PLAYING\' : this.state.mode\n```\n\nWait — even simpler: after handleRedo, the mode is finalized (REPLAYING or GAME_OVER). So:\n\n```ts\nif (mode === \'REPLAYING\') {\n  await this.handleRedo()\n\n  // The replay is over. If the final move ended the game,\n  // keep the game-over screen, otherwise hand control back\n  // to the player\n  if (wellStateId + 1 in replay) {\n    nextReplayTimeoutId = setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)\n  } else if (this.state.mode === \'REPLAYING\') {\n    nextMode = \'PLAYING\'\n  }\n}\n...\nthis.setState({\n  mode: nextMode === mode ? this.state.mode : nextMode\n})\n```\n\nUgly. Cleaner: don\'t track nextMode at all. Compute it only when transitioning:\n\n```ts\nhandleReplayTimeout = async () => {\n  const { replayTimeout } = this.props\n  const { mode, replay, wellStateId } = this.state\n\n  let nextReplayTimeoutId\n\n  if (mode === \'REPLAYING\') {\n    await this.handleRedo()\n\n    if (wellStateId + 1 in replay) {\n      nextReplayTimeoutId = setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)\n    } else if (this.state.mode === \'REPLAYING\') {\n      // The replay is over and the game isn\'t: hand control\n      // back to the player\n      this.setState({ mode: \'PLAYING\' })\n    }\n  } else {\n    console.warn(\'Ignoring input replay step because mode is\', mode)\n  }\n\n  this.setState({\n    replayTimeoutId: nextReplayTimeoutId\n  })\n}\n```\n\nTwo setStates (batched by React 18+? Inside a timeout (not an event) — React 18\'s automatic batching batches all updates including timeouts. So they merge into one render.) This way I never touch mode except for the REPLAYING→PLAYING transition, and no overwrite risk.\n\nCoverage: the else-if is the same as before.\n\n2. {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'Clean. Task complete. Summary:\n\n**Root cause**: When a replay ran out of moves (when `wellStateId + 1 in replay` was false), `handleReplayTimeout` stopped scheduling the next timeout, but the mode remained `REPLAYING` forever. All input handlers (`handleLeft/Right/Up/Down`) ignore input unless the mode is `PLAYING` — so after an incomplete replay, the game became unresponsive until a page refresh.\n\n**Secondary root cause found during verification**: The first fix attempt read `this.state.mode` after `await this.handleRedo()` to distinguish "game ended on the last move" from "game still alive" — but in React 19, the `setState` from `handleRedo` is not flushed before that read, so on a replay that ends the game, `this.state.mode` was still the stale `REPLAYING`, and the transition was overwriting `GAME_OVER` with `PLAYING` (the well ended up in a game-over state with a `null` piece → subsequent input crashed with "Can\'t get next well state if there is no piece in the well"). Final fix: a functional `setState` updater, which React guarantees to evaluate against the latest state.\n\n**Files changed**:\n- `src/components/Game/Game.tsx` — `handleReplayTimeout`: when the replay runs out and the game is still alive, set `mode: \'PLAYING\'`.\n- `test/components/Game/Game.test.tsx` — 2 regression tests:\n  1. "lets you continue playing once an incomplete replay runs out of moves" — replays a single `D` (the bug-report scenario), verifies the "replaying..." indicator disappears and that a subsequent `{Down}` is actually played (down button count 0 → 1, no warnings). Fails before the fix.\n  2. "keeps the game over screen when a complete replay ends the game on its last move" — replays the 187-move lovetris game that ends on the last move, verifies the game-over screen (`replay-out`) is preserved and the mode is not clobbered to PLAYING. This guards against the stale-state regression.\n  (Both tests capture DOM values before unmounting and then assert — if you assert while a game in a buggy state is still mounted, the failing async game activity keeps the Node process alive, and the suite hangs instead of reporting.)\n\n**Verification**:\n- Test 1 fails before the fix (`ERR_ASSERTION: ... expected null, got \'replaying...\'` div), passes after the fix.\n- `npm run unit`: full suite green, 100% line/branch/function coverage (the repo\'s enforced gate), exit 0.\n- Confirmed via a standalone logic simulation that the 187-move lovetris D-spam replay indeed ends the game exactly on move 187, and confirmed that the pre-fix behavior (mode clobbering → null-piece crash) was real and has been resolved.\n', 'thinkingSignature': 'reasoning'}, {'type': 'text', 'text': '\n\nDone. Summary:\n\n## Root cause\n\n`handleReplayTimeout` in `src/components/Game/Game.tsx` scheduled the next replay step only while `wellStateId + 1 in replay`. When an incomplete replay (e.g. `D`) ran out of moves, the chain stopped but `mode` stayed `REPLAYING` forever — and every input handler (`handleLeft/Right/Up/Down`) ignores input unless `mode === \'PLAYING\'`. Result: softlock until refresh, exactly as reported.\n\nA second, subtler cause surfaced while verifying the fix: the first attempt distinguished "game ended on the last move" by reading `this.state.mode` right after `await this.handleRedo()` — but React 19 doesn\'t flush that `setState` before the read, so the value was stale `REPLAYING`. On a replay that ends the game, this overwrote `GAME_OVER` with `PLAYING`, leaving the well in a game-over state with `piece === null`; the next keypress then crashed with "Can\'t get next well state if there is no piece in the well".\n\n## Fix (src/components/Game/Game.tsx, `handleReplayTimeout`)\n\nWhen the replay is exhausted, transition to `PLAYING` via a **functional `setState` updater** — React guarantees the updater sees the post-`handleRedo` state, so `GAME_OVER` set by the final move is preserved:\n\n```ts\n} else {\n  // The replay is over. If the game didn\'t end\n  // on its last move, hand control back to the player\n  this.setState(state => state.mode === \'REPLAYING\'\n    ? { mode: \'PLAYING\' }\n    : state)\n}\n```\n\n## Tests (test/components/Game/Game.test.tsx)\n\n1. **"lets you continue playing once an incomplete replay runs out of moves"** — the bug report\'s scenario: replays a single `D`, asserts the "replaying..." indicator disappears and a subsequent `{Down}` is actually played. **Failed before the fix** (`expected null, got \'replaying…\'`), passes after.\n2. **"keeps the game over screen when a complete replay ends the game on its last move"** — replays the 187-move lovetris D-spam game (verified by standalone logic simulation that it ends the game on exactly move 187) and asserts the game-over screen is retained — guards the stale-mode clobbering regression.\n\nBoth tests capture DOM values, unmount, then assert: asserting while a buggily-mounted game is still active leaves async activity that keeps the Node process alive, hanging the suite instead of reporting the failure.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `npm run unit`: full suite green — 19/19 `<Game>` tests, **100% line/branch/function coverage** (the repo\'s enforced gate), exit 0.\n- No unrelated tests modified or deleted; debug scratch file removed.'}], 'api': 'openai-completions', 'provider': 'pod-qwen-medium', 'model': 'qwen3.8-27b-bf16', 'usage': {'input': 61745, 'output': 1277, 'cacheRead': 0, 'cacheWrite': 0, 'totalTokens': 63022, 'cost': {'input': 0, 'output': 0, 'cacheRead': 0, 'cacheWrite': 0, 'total': 0}}, 'stopReason': 'stop', 'timestamp': 1787276842315, 'responseId': 'chatcmpl-8cf88e1499257136', 'duration': 49718.124799999874, 'ttft': 14309.995200000238, 'contextSnapshot': {'promptTokens': 61745, 'nonMessageTokens': 6752}}
